title: Transition from principles to the law of sacrifices
english: We have spoken already about the principles of Leviticus; now we come to the law of the sacrifices that are called gifts. The soul which has sinned from among the people—not always by will, but by ignorance—offers a gift. The synagogue and the soul are read as figures.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen has just finished the moral application of the burnt offering and now turns to the law of sacrifices, called 'gifts,' beginning with the soul that sins from ignorance.

title: The poor person's offering of fine flour
english: A gift of fine flour with oil and frankincense means praise and prayer. The priest burns the memorial portion. The one who cannot offer an animal offers flour: mercy acknowledges the degrees of poverty.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the graduated offerings in Leviticus, now turning to the offering of fine flour with oil and frankincense as the sacrifice of the poor.

title: Degrees of sacrifice match degrees of sin
english: If the whole synagogue has gone astray, they offer a calf. One soul goes astray—a goat or a sheep is offered. The degree of sin is the degree of the victim. Christ is for the people and for individuals.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining how the size of the sin offering in Leviticus corresponds to the scope of the sin: the whole congregation offers a calf, while an individual soul offers a goat or sheep.

title: Blood at the altar, skin and dung burned outside
english: The blood goes on the altar; the skin and the dung are burned outside the camp. Christ suffered outside the gate (Hebrews 13:12). We carry his reproach (Hebrews 13:13).
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the disposal of the sin-offering's parts, applying the burning outside the camp to Christ's suffering outside the gate.

title: The priest eats the sin offering in the holy place
english: The priest eats the sacrifice of sin in the holy place (Leviticus 6:26). The one who carries the sins of the people is made holy. Christ is our food; he carried our sin. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET: no ANF; do not copy Barkley FOTC 83.
orientation: Origen is explaining the sin offering, having just spoken of Christ suffering outside the gate and bearing our reproach.
